test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2024: Official Paper (Held On: 05 Jul, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The teacher will never / give you punishment / if you will / come on time.
solution:
The correct answer is** Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the phrase 'if you will' is incorrect.
 
• In conditional sentences, the simple present tense is used in the **condition clause (after 'if').**
 
• The correct construction should be 'if you come'.
 
• **Example:** *If you come on time, the teacher will never give you punishment*.

Hence, the correct statement is: ***The teacher will never give you punishment if you come on time__*__.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• In conditional sentences, when the condition clause (if-clause) is in the simple present tense, the result clause (main clause) is usually in the simple future tense.

 
 
• **Example:** *If it **rains**, we** will stay** indoors*.
 
 
 
• Do not use the future tense in the if-clause.
 
 
• Incorrect: *If you will come on time, we will start the meeting*.
 
• Correct: ***If you come on time, we will start the meeting*****.**
